# Data audit (generated by `python -m src.audit`)

- **Rows / columns:** 250,000 / 23
- **Missing values (total cells):** 0
- **Rows with non-positive size or price:** 0
- **Missing required columns:** none
- **Duplicate rows ignoring ID:** 0
- **Date consistency:** Age_of_Property + Year_Built takes values [2025] (reference year 2025); Year_Built range 1990-2023. The pipeline recomputes age from Year_Built against this single reference year.
- **Floor_No > Total_Floors:** 116,304 rows (46.5%) - impossible physically; kept and flagged via `Floor_Inconsistent`, ratio capped at 1. Dropping them would discard almost half the data; repairing them would invent data.
- **Floor_No == 0 (ground floor):** 8,203 rows - valid
- **Source Price_per_SqFt:** in lakhs, rounded to 2 dp (2,534 rows are 0.0, max rounding error 0.005 lakh/sqft); recomputed in rupees/sqft as `Price_per_SqFt_Rs`.
- **Locality ids:** 500 ids; 500 appear in more than one city (median 42 cities) -> not a geographic hierarchy; excluded from models.
- **City -> State:** 0 cities map to more than one state (consistent)
- **Amenity tokens:** {'Garden': 150177, 'Pool': 150096, 'Clubhouse': 150059, 'Gym': 149960, 'Playground': 149780}
- **Largest |correlation| among raw numeric attributes:** 0.0059 -> columns look independent (synthetic).
- **Corr(price, size):** -0.0025

## Synthetic patterns and implausible combinations

- **Near-uniform numeric columns (KS distance to uniform; 0 = perfectly uniform):** {'Size_in_SqFt': 0.0014, 'Price_in_Lakhs': 0.003, 'Year_Built': 0.0303}
- **Category shares (min-max):** {'State': '4.9%-5.1%', 'Property_Type': '33.2%-33.5%', 'BHK': '19.9%-20.1%', 'Furnished_Status': '33.3%-33.4%', 'Facing': '24.9%-25.1%', 'Owner_Type': '33.3%-33.4%', 'Availability_Status': '50.0%-50.0%'} -> near-perfectly balanced, unlike real listings
- **BHK vs size:** corr -0.001; 22,355 one-BHK listings of 3,000+ sq ft; 3,409 five-BHK listings of 800 sq ft or less; sq ft per BHK spans 100-5000
- **Under_Construction vs build year:** 125,035 under-construction listings have Year_Built 1990-2023; 77,128 were 'built' in 2010 or earlier - contradictory
- **Houses/villas in tall buildings:** 150,227 of 167,044 houses/villas have Total_Floors > 3
- **Price per sq ft (INR):** range 202-99,182; 3.7% of rows under 1,000 and 2.9% over 50,000
- **Variance in price explained by (eta squared):** {'City': 0.00019, 'State': 0.0001, 'Property_Type': 2e-05, 'BHK': 0.0, 'Furnished_Status': 0.0, 'Availability_Status': 1e-05}

## Fixes applied vs. issues that cannot be fixed

**Applied (safe, nothing invented):** exact-duplicate check (none found); source price per sq ft recomputed in INR; age recomputed from Year_Built against one reference year; impossible floors flagged (`Floor_Inconsistent`) with the ratio capped, rows kept; app input validation and warnings for floors, future build years, out-of-range values, under-construction/old-building and unusual size-per-BHK entries.

**Not fixable without better data:** the uniform/balanced distributions, the lack of any BHK-size or price-attribute relationship, under-construction listings with old build years, houses in tall buildings, extreme price per sq ft values. Dropping or 'repairing' these rows would either discard most of the data or fabricate values, so they are retained and disclosed. Conclusions drawn from this data describe the dataset, not real markets.

## Consequence

Price is statistically unrelated to every other attribute, so a regressor cannot learn price from them and real-market conclusions cannot be drawn. No future-price or investment-outcome column exists, so the 5-year price and 'good investment' label are assumption/rule based.
